title: Contrastive Hypergraph Source-free Domain Adaptive Object Detection in Adverse Weathers
claim: Pairwise relations connect too few samples and collapse under degradation; grouping samples into hyperedges adds context and propagates semantics.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; right panel splits pairwise vs hypergraph with dashed divider
description: The figure has two main panels. The left panel, 'Traditional Methods', shows a vertical flow. A padlock with a red X over a street photo marks inaccessible source data D_s. Arrows lead to a pre-trained model f_theta, then to 'Results on Target Domain': three street images (snow, orange night, fog) with dashed detection boxes. The right panel, 'Pairwise vs. Hypergraph Solution', is split by a dashed vertical line. On the left of it, a gray 'Pairwise Graph (Limited Context)' shows scattered blurry orange and blue dots joined by thin lines. A red X marks a bad link, and labels note limited connectivity and agreement collapse. On the right, a peach 'Hypergraph Reunion (Ours)' header sits over colored blobs: purple intra-image context, green cross-condition context with a clear-weather car, and yellow appearance similarity. A net shape ties the blobs together. The eye goes first to the bold panel titles, then to the red X and the colorful hyperedge regions.
caption: In SFDA, source data is inaccessible, while target images suffer from structured degradation (e.g., fog, rain, night), leading to detection collapse. Existing pairwise contrastive methods fail in such noisy settings. \framework builds a contrastive hypergraph over object proposals using multi-relation hyperedges (e.g., intra-image context, and cross-condition views) to propagate semantics from confident to low-contrast instances.
abstract: Adverse weather conditions such as fog, rain, snow, and low illumination introduce structured visibility degradations that severely impair object detectors trained on clear-weather data. When source data is inaccessible due to privacy or transmission constraints, source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) becomes necessary; however, existing SFDA methods based on pairwise contrastive learning struggle to capture high-order semantics and often suffer from agreement collapse under severe corruption. We propose REUNION, a hypergraph-guided SFDA framework for object detection under adverse weather. REUNION constructs a contrastive hypergraph over target-domain object proposals, encoding high-order relations through intra-image context, weather-aware grouping, prototype-based semantic anchors, and uncertainty-aware connections between reliable and low-confidence instances. To effectively exploit these structured relations, we introduce a group-wise Hyper-InfoNCE objective that optimizes representations at the hyperedge level, enabling semantic information to propagate from confident proposals to corrupted or low-contrast instances. Experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that REUNION effectively mitigates domain shifts and achieves state-of-the-art performance in SFDA settings.
